A flintlock mana pistol handed down among witches.\n\nBy charging its bullets with magic beforehand, even those of weak or meager magic can achieve a set level of power. Those of high skill and practiced hands can draw out power to match.

A long-range rifle of Church origin, adorned with beautiful ornamentation.\n\nImbued with holy power, it is formidable, but most remarkable is its penetrating force, able to pierce through many demons at once.

A secret art handed down among witches: a giant crest sword that calls down lightning.\n\nLightning falls a few seconds after casting; strike the sword with lightning in the meantime and it stores power, increasing the strength and number of bolts.
A Dark art that sets a trap which summons an iron maiden.\n\nAn application of transference magic. Summoning a great torture device from a tiny trap is a pairing that could hardly be more fitting.
A Dark art that turns one's own loathsome darkness into dark flame and unleashes it at great speed.\n\nDark sorcerers devised this art by focusing on the darkness that lurks in human hearts.

An art that hurls a pot of sinister contents forward.

Besides the explosion, a recovery orb appears if your "Luck" is good.
This peculiar art is said to have been made by a witch fair of face but catastrophically unable to cook.

An art that creates an orb of light which, when collected, restores MP at the cost of HP.\n\nFor a sorcerer, magic takes priority above all else; it is said none are more useless than a sorcerer whose magic has run dry.

A Church art that hurls a cross forward and then detonates it.

The blast holds holy power; catching enemies in it releases orbs that restore HP.
A favorite art of Candore, perhaps meant also as a rite of mourning.

A sword technique derived from the Church that unleashes a holy slash tracing a cross.

It can be performed without any weapon, but wielding it requires considerable Intelligence.
Rumor has it that it was devised not by a Church knight or a sorcerer, but by a mere maid.
Creates a shining wall ahead that bars the enemy's approach.\n\nUsed to nullify certain attacks or to break away from enemies and regroup.
A short-range shotgun of Church origin with a flamboyant design.\n\nIts range is short and its shot spreads, so it is useful only up close, but in melee it will prove a reassuring ally.

A cannon that fires enormous crest shells.

It is practically an antique, yet its simple construction lets it be used without trouble.
A portable refit of those used in the last great war against the demons, it delivers a tremendous impact on hit.

A simple art that lets you instantly use a Talisman in your possession.

By charging it with magic through the art beforehand, it becomes easier to use than as a mere item.
In all things, it is the split-second decision that divides life and death.

An art that conjures a fireball and hurls it forward.

Fire lies at the root of human life, and fire arts are said to be the first ever developed.
Quick and easy to use, it remains in use even by high-ranking sorcerers.

A Fire art created by the Flame Witch faction to carve their own way into enemy ranks.

It has little power and will not make foes flinch, but can cancel out lesser projectiles.
Though sorcerers, they excelled at close combat while cloaked in multiple arts.

A special black powder mist that explodes in response to magic or projectiles.

Fire magic in particular triggers a larger blast than usual.
To master it without being caught in the blast, one must mind one's footing.

A Witchcraft spell that calls down lightning at a fixed distance ahead.

Its range is narrow, but it activates quickly and is easy to handle.
Often learned as a basic of Witchcraft, it is known by many witches.

A Witchcraft spell that unleashes lightning several times at fixed intervals.

Combining it with normal attacks or other spells after casting builds stagger quickly, making foes easy to flinch.
A fairly advanced spell; few witches can wield it well.
